geometry.locator: RNO_season_2022.json (commit 008d623) station 11 pos_easting/pos_northing; rnog_detector.py origin; arXiv:2411.12922 Figure 1 shows station 11 (Nanoq) west/north of the DISC borehole (viewed, not traced)
geometry.note: Derived from collaboration-published offsets and a published origin; the offsets are as-installed positions (depth wrt snow level at time of measurement) from the detector description, not a separate survey table. Spacings to neighbouring stations pass the 1.25 km grid check within 5 %.

method: Computed: station 11's published offsets (easting -1572.9 m, northing 730.0 m, pos_site 'summit') from the RNO_season_2022.json detector description were added to the published origin (72.582793 N, -38.455815 E, the DISC borehole) in a spherical local tangent plane (R = 6 371 008.8 m; dlat = N/R, dlon = E/(R cos 72.582793 deg)), giving 72.5893581 N, -38.5030726 E. The offsets are taken as true-east/true-north metres; if the collaboration's easting/northing axes are grid-aligned instead (UTM zone 24 convergence is about 0.5 degrees here), stations 4 km north of the origin would move by up to about 40 m, hence accuracy_m 100.
name: RNO-G station 11 (Nanoq)
notes: Station 11 commissioning month (2021-07) is the 'commission_time' in the detector description; the station's three 100 m strings and nine surface antennas lie within a few tens of metres of this point.

summary.plain: RNO-G station 11 (Nanoq), one of the seven radio-detector stations of the Radio Neutrino Observatory in Greenland, placed on the ice sheet to the north and north-west of the Summit Station camp.
